issues.failure_explanation: The displayed item (i) is false for p>1. The proof uses the lower bound on |x| to infer |hλ|^p ≤ h^p rad(V0)^p + ∫|x|^p dμ over the cell, but this does not follow for p>1. Counterexample: d=1, Λ=Z, V0=[-1/2,1/2), h=1, μ=δ_{9.5}. Then μ(V_{10})=1, M_2(μ)=9.5^2=90.25, LHS=10^2=100, while RHS=0.5^2+90.25=90.5.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace item (i) by the triangle-inequality bound ∑ |hλ|^p μ(V_{hλ}) ≤ 2^{p-1}(M_p(μ)+h^p rad(V0)^p), or add an appropriate constant, and adjust the subsequent finite-moment estimates.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's item (i) is false, so the finite-moment arguments in THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac and THM:LatticePiecewiseConstant are unsupported. Their main W_p approximation bounds can still be recovered with constant adjustments.
issues.title: False radial estimate in Lemma LEM:RadialEstimates
issues.why_classification: The false estimate is a local technical inequality; a standard constant-adjusted repair preserves all substantive approximation rates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that for any $h\in(0,1]$, $\mu_h$ has at most \[\mc{N}(B_R,hV_{0}) \leq 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}(B_R,V_0) = 3^dh^{-d}\mc{N}\] terms

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the number of nonzero terms by N(B_R,hV0), but this covering number can be smaller than the number of lattice cells intersecting B_R. Moreover, for small N, h=3(N/N)^{1/d} can exceed 1, so Lemma LEM:CoveringNumber (valid only for h∈(0,1]) is inapplicable. Counterexample: d=2, V0 a 1000×0.001 rectangle from a rectangular lattice, B_R the unit ball, N≈2000, N=1 gives h≈134. The support ball intersects about 15 cells of hV0, so μ_h has about 15 terms, not at most 1.

failure_location.quote: Then $\mu_h = \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \mu(V_{h\lambda})\delta_{h\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation of $\mu$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition N≥27 N(B_R,V0) (so h≤1) and replace the term-count step by a correct bound on the number of lattice cells intersecting B_R, using the factor 3 slack to retain at most N terms.
issues.overall_effect: The all-N N-term guarantee in THM:NTermDirac and COR:NTermPiecewiseConstant fails for small N or anisotropic lattices. The asymptotic O(N^{-1/d}) rate can be recovered by requiring N sufficiently large so h≤1.
issues.title: THM:NTermDirac N-term guarantee fails for small N / h>1
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as stated for small N, but the intended asymptotic N-term rate survives under a standard large-N condition; no major loss of rate or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Setting $h=N^{-\frac1d}$ yields $N$ cubes of length $N^{-\frac1d}$ in the unit cube

issues.failure_explanation: For the unit cube [-1/2,1/2]^d and Λ_N=(N^{-1/d}Z)^d, the Voronoi cells do not partition the cube into N cells. They intersect the cube in (N^{1/d}+1)^d cells. For d=1, N=2, h=0.5, the cells centered at -0.5, 0, and 0.5 all intersect the interior, so μ_N can have 3 nonzero terms, not at most 2.

failure_location.quote: Then $\mu_N = \sum_{\lambda\in\Lambda_N}\mu(V_{\lambda})\delta_{\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation to $\mu$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Shift the lattice so the Voronoi cells align with the unit cube, or choose h=(N^{1/d}-1)^{-1} (or similar) to ensure at most N cells intersect the support; adjust constants.
issues.overall_effect: The exact at-most-N pixel corollaries are false. The N^{-1/d} rate can be recovered by shifting the lattice or reducing h, but the stated constants and at-most-N claim fail.
issues.title: Unit-cube pixel corollary has too many lattice cells
issues.why_classification: The corollary's exact N-term guarantee fails, but a standard shift/scaling repair preserves the N^{-1/d} rate and the structured approximation.

issues.failure_explanation: The sum bound ∑_{j≥floor R} 1/(j+1-R)^2 ≤ π^2/6 holds only when R is an integer. If R=0.5, floor R=0, the sum is ∑_{j=0}∞ 1/(j+0.5)^2 = π^2/2. Thus the constant 6/π^2 is too large; I2 can be as large as ε^p rather than ε^p/3, so the total can exceed ε^p and W_p(μ, \hatμ)<ε is not guaranteed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the constant 6/π^2 in assumption 2 to a constant that bounds the actual sum, e.g., 2/π^2, or define the shell decay using ∑_{j≥floor R}(j+1-R)^{-2}.
issues.overall_effect: The noncompact extension theorem's stated decay condition is insufficient to guarantee W_p<ε. The qualitative noncompact result survives with a stronger constant.
issues.title: Incorrect annulus sum constant in THM:noncompact_ext
issues.why_classification: The defect is a constant factor in the decay assumption; a one-line constant correction preserves the noncompact approximation result and its scope.
